title: Telemetry Chronicle: TTL, Tenant Provenance & Access Ledger
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a tenant-aware telemetry chronicle that provides deterministic TTL enforcement, immutable tenant provenance metadata, and an access ledger for all reads of trace/metrics/log slices. This ticket covers schema changes, ingestion-path tagging, store-side TTL enforcement, RBAC checks on read endpoints, and an append-only access ledger for auditability.

Why: Recent incident (INC-2026-11) revealed gaps in tenant-level retention and inability to prove who viewed sensitive trace payloads. We need a single cohesive solution that: 1) associates a tamper-evident provenance blob with each telemetry item (trace span, log event, metric sample); 2) enforces configurable TTLs via the storage layer rather than ad-hoc retention jobs; and 3) records read events with requester identity, purpose, and query context for compliance audits.

Acceptance criteria:
- Schema: All ingested telemetry includes provenance fields: tenant_id, tenant_affinity_token (rotated), provenance_version, and sensitivity_label. Schema change documented in Confluence and backward-compatible.
- Ingestion: Collector/ingest pipeline tags items with tenant-affinity token; tokens are resolved via control plane lookup. Ingest path rejects telemetry without tenant context for private deployments.
- TTL enforcement: Storage layer (blobstore/TSDB/archive) enforces TTL per-tenant-per-data-class (trace/log/metric) with max/min guards. Scheduled retention jobs removed for data classes migrated.
- Access ledger: Every read through the Query API (Grafana datasource, internal replay tool, debug endpoints) appends an immutable ledger entry: requestor, method, query_hash, time_window, filters, redaction_policy_applied. Ledger entries are exportable and searchable by audit team.
- RBAC: Query endpoints perform tenant-scoped RBAC—cross-tenant queries require elevated access and produce high-severity audit logs.
- PII redaction: Sensitive fields flagged by sensitivity_label are auto-masked in non-authorized reads; just-in-time unmasking requires explicit approval and creates a separate ledger record.
- Dashboards: Add observability dashboards showing TTL enforcement coverage, ledger write rate, failed RBAC checks, and unmasking requests.
- Tests: Integration tests that simulate tenant rotation, TTL expiry, ledger writes, and RBAC enforcement. Performance regression <5% on ingest path at 95th percentile.

Design/Implementation notes:
- Use provenance blob signed with service KMS key to make tamper-evident; rotate per-tenant tokens quarterly. Provenance format: base64 JSON (tenant_id, issuance_ts, token_id, signing_key_id, schema_version).
- TTL stored as metadata at object level for blobstore and as column TTL for TSDB shards where supported. For append-only object archives, a background compaction worker will reconcile object TTLs and trigger permanent deletion jobs.
- Access ledger implemented as append-only Kafka topic with a compacted index in DynamoDB for quick audit queries. Ledger entries are small (<=1 KB) and encrypted at rest.
- RBAC enforcement hooks to be added to query gateway; upstream services must pass an identity token and purpose string. Gateway will validate against the Access Policy Service (APS) and reject or transform results based on policy.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag the provenance enrichment in the ingest pipeline (start as opt-in for internal tenants).
2) Deploy read-path ledger hook in readonly mode (writes to topic but marked dry-run) for 2 weeks, validate volume and schema.
3) Enable TTL metadata writes and run reconciliation in dry-run to measure deletions.
4) Flip enforcement for non-production tenants, then production tenants with accelerated telemetry sampling.
5) Monitor dashboards and involve security for sign-off.

Monitoring & Alerts:
- Alert if ledger write success <99.9% over 10m.
- Alert if TTL reconciliation backlog > 1M objects.
- Dashboard panels: Ledger QPS, per-tenant avg ledger entries/day, failed RBAC denied/sec, unmasking approvals by approver, TTL expirations by data-class.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Telemetry+Chronicle+Design
- Proto schema: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-protos/pull/98
- Draft Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs/telemetry-chronicle
- Incident note: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-11

Open questions/Trade-offs:
- Ledger storage cost vs query latency: full retention of ledger in hot store increases cost. Proposal: keep 90 days hot then cold archive; audit queries beyond 90 days run as batch jobs.
- Signed provenance vs hashed token: signing allows tamper-evidence but complicates rotation. Decided to sign with KMS and include key_id for rotation.
- TTL enforcement location: store-level enforcement preferred for determinism; requires modifications to several storage adapters (S3-layer TTL tags, TSDB TTL columns).
